source.original_title: 05/27/2026 - Ram Bala x Harry Edmonds KL
source.display_title: 05/27/2026 - Ram Bala x Harry Edmonds KL — Follow Up

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: 'i know you spoke with kyla um yes gave me she gave me like a head start' and the prospect: 'same thing as what I told Kayla'

prospect.name: Ram Bala
prospect.occupation: IT consultant — 'I have always been a IT consultant all my life'; works from a home office
prospect.family_status: Two sons, 19 and 14; family visiting during his June travel
prospect.training_background: Used to do HIIT classes including kickboxing/kicks; stopped training in December/January and has not trained for five months. Gym-experienced with barbells and dumbbells but trains only seated lower-body machines (leg extensions, knee lifts) and will not squat with weight on his back. Has never used kettlebells. Vegetarian; currently eating ~1,500 kcal/day, down from 2,400-2,500.
prospect.medical: Chronic stiff lower back; disc bulge diagnosed around 2010, treated with traction and massage. Stiffens badly after standing two hours or more and he goes to a chiropractor for adjustments. Explicitly fearful of loading the spine: 'does it concern me when I'm lifting weights? Yes, 100%'. Down from 230 lb to ~202 lb (103 kg to 92 kg) over five months by diet alone; body fat measured at 22% at a chiropractic wellness check, which surprised him.

signals: Systematically comparison-shopping: 'third person I'm speaking to... this is the third quote as well' and another provider booked for the following week
Hard price anchor from a like-for-like competitor: 'the most expensive quote I've received is $2,000 for one year'
Analytical, consultant-style evaluation of the purchase — frames it as scope, budget and time variables

Counter-signal: not self-directed on the training itself — he explicitly will not train his lower body alone and wants supervision, which is closer to the_medically_constrained on motive even though the buying behaviour is bargain-hunter

goals.text: Lose about 10% body fat from 22% and get visible abs and definition
Pack on muscle after losing weight and muscle together over five months off
Fix the lower-back mobility so it stops being the thing that blocks everything else
Train his lower body safely — the thing he will not do alone at the gym
Keep up with his two sons, 19 and 14 — 'It's a matter of time. I got to keep up. I'm 45 now.'
Make a visible and mental difference before the end of 2026

pains.text: Disc bulge and chronic lower-back stiffness since 2010 requiring chiropractic adjustments
Afraid to load his back — will not squat with weight and avoids all standing lower-body work
Has not trained at all for five months despite intending to the whole time — 'I'm sitting wanting to do things and it's five months past'
Falls out of traditional and HIIT programmes because results take too long
Will not train alone without a trainer or spotter, and depending on friends makes it inconsistent
Lost muscle along with the fat during the layoff — 22% body fat despite dropping 25 lb
Sits in a home office all day, which he links to not using his core, glutes or hamstrings
Busy with work and expects to stay busy

objections.raw_quote: That's the most expensive I've ever heard
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it happens, then clarified the meaning — 'When you say steep, do you mean like, you don't think it's worth it, or you just weren't expecting it?' — and justified the price on Trevor being top of category

objections.raw_quote: the most expensive quote I've received is $2,000 for one year
objections.rep_response: Asked the strongest available question — 'why didn't you do the one that was 2K for a year?' — accepted the answer that he was still evaluating, then framed it as money-versus-certainty and explicitly declined to decide for him

objections.raw_quote: it's just comes down to the cost aspect of it, which I need to kind of figure that out and digest
objections.rep_response: Time-boxed it — 'How long do you feel like you need to wrap your head around things?' — and pre-solved the travel logistics by offering to onboard him before he leaves

offer.payment_plan_terms: Explicitly refused when asked. Prospect: 'are we gonna do this month on month or three months and three months or one, six months, one shot?' Rep: 'It's six months, one shot.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'We guarantee the results... by the end of the six months, you will be doing an extra 20 pounds from your starting weight on all of the main lifts with the same intensity, same volume, same reps... And the guarantee is that if you're not there in six months, we work with you for free until you are there.'

evidence: No decision, no payment, no link sent. 'let me work that out' and 'I need to kind of figure that out and digest'
Real intent and a deadline he set himself: 'I want to finalize before I leave' (he travels 4-26 June) and 'one way or the other, I'll let you know... I'm not going to keep you hanging'
Contact method agreed — he will reach out on the number the rep texts from
Counter-evidence: he has a $2,000/year alternative quote in hand and a fourth provider call booked for the following week, and he twice called the price steep
Counter-evidence: no follow-up call was booked and no date was agreed; the next move is entirely his
outcome.next_step: Prospect to decide before he travels on 4 June and contact the rep by text; rep offered to complete onboarding and the Trevor call before departure

notable.note: Two things a principal should see. First, the rep told this prospect flatly that payment is 'six months, one shot' when directly asked about instalments — the day after telling another prospect that payments can be broken up through third parties. Second, the prospect asked about the group programme that the setter Kyla had raised with him, and was steered off it on clinical grounds without ever being told what it costs. He also has a disc bulge, sees a chiropractor, and asked whether blood work was needed before starting; he was told it was not necessary.

quality.notes: The opening two minutes and several long stretches (00:06:43-00:08:30, 00:20:54-00:27:27, 00:36:08 onward) are merged blocks where both speakers' words sit under one label — the entire philosophy pitch is attributed to the rep but contains the prospect's replies, and the price reveal at 00:36:46-00:37:04 flips between labels mid-exchange. Roles resolved from content.
